title: Europe in 1100: The Age of the First Crusade
caption: Europe in 1100, the age of the First Crusade: the Holy Roman Empire fills the middle, Norman England and Norman Italy sit at opposite ends, and Kiev is one of many Rus' principalities.

title: Europe in 1200: The High Middle Ages
caption: Europe in 1200: the Angevin Empire stretches across England and western France, Iberia is split between Christian kingdoms and the Almohad Caliphate, and Rus' is a patchwork of principalities.

title: Europe in 1250: After the Mongol Invasion
caption: Europe in 1250, after the Mongol invasion: the Golden Horde now covers the east, Lithuania is rising, and Byzantium is split into rival successor states like Nicaea and Epirus.

title: Europe in 1350: The Years of the Black Death
caption: Europe in 1350, the years of the Black Death. Borders barely moved, but the Golden Horde, Lithuania and the Holy Roman Empire still dominate the map while the Ottomans appear in Anatolia.

title: Europe in 1400: The Late Middle Ages
caption: Europe in 1400: Lithuania is one of the biggest states on the map, the Kalmar Union joins Scandinavia, and the Ottoman Empire already holds much of the Balkans.

title: Europe in 1453: The Fall of Constantinople
caption: Europe in 1453, the year Constantinople fell. Look how little of the Byzantine Empire is left on this map, while the Ottoman Empire spreads across the Balkans and Poland-Lithuania dominates the east.

title: Europe in 1492: The Year Columbus Sailed
caption: Europe in 1492, the year Columbus sailed. Spain is still two kingdoms, Castile and Aragon, Granada is gone, and Muscovy and Poland-Lithuania now face each other across the east.

title: Europe in 1600: The Age of Empires
caption: Europe in 1600: the Spanish Empire covers Iberia and much of Italy, Russia stretches across the east, and the Ottomans hold the Balkans. The Dutch are a small orange sliver on the coast.

title: Europe in 1783: Before the French Revolution
caption: Europe in 1783, six years before the French Revolution: Great Britain and France face the Habsburgs, Prussia and Russia, and Poland-Lithuania is shrinking on the map.

title: Europe in 1878: After the Congress of Berlin
caption: Europe in 1878, after the Congress of Berlin: Romania, Serbia and Montenegro are independent, Bulgaria and Eastern Rumelia appear, and the German Empire and Austria-Hungary sit in the middle.

title: Europe in 1900: At the Turn of the Century
caption: Europe in 1900: the German Empire, Austria-Hungary and the Russian Empire dominate the continent, the Ottomans still hold the southern Balkans, and Sweden-Norway is still one union.

title: Europe in 1925: Between the World Wars
caption: Europe in 1925: new states fill the gap where empires stood. Poland, Czechoslovakia, Finland, the Baltic states and the Kingdom of Serbs, Croats and Slovenes are all on the map.

title: Europe in 1937: On the Eve of World War II
caption: Europe in 1937, two years before the war: Yugoslavia has replaced the old Kingdom of Serbs, Croats and Slovenes, Czechoslovakia and Poland still stand, and Ireland now appears on the map.

title: New Countries Born After the Fall of the Iron Curtain
caption: Born after the Iron Curtain fell: Germany reunified in 1990, then the Soviet Union and Yugoslavia broke up and Czechoslovakia split in 1993. How many red countries can you name?

title: Who Fought in WWI and When They Joined

title: Europe in 1939: After the Partition of Poland
caption: Europe in 1939, after the partition of Poland: the Greater German Reich and the Soviet Union now meet where Poland was, and Slovakia and Bohemia-Moravia appear as new entities.

title: Europe in 1940: After the Fall of France
caption: Europe in 1940, after the fall of France: the map shows Occupied France in the north and Vichy France in the south, with Denmark, Norway and the Low Countries now under German control.

title: Europe in 1942: At the Height of Axis Expansion
